title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page continues Grothendieck's analysis of a profinite group generated by two torsion elements, ρ and σ. The model is SL(2,Z) ⊂ GL(2,Z) viewed as an amalgam Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6: σ has order 4 and ρ order 6, with σ^2 = ρ^3 = -1 central. Notation: G_{ρ,σ} is the ambient (GL2-like) group and 𝔊 ⊂ G_{ρ,σ} the SL2-like part. τ is an element with τρτ^{-1} = ρ^{-1}; the previous page introduces τ' = σ^{-1}τ, corresponding to the matrix (0 1; 1 0). χ is the 'determinant' character, with 𝔊 = ker χ, and 𝔊' contains 𝔊 with index 2 (the GL2-like part generated by 𝔊 and τ). μ ∈ Ẑ^× is the cyclotomic-type parameter. ε_3(μ) = ±1 is the character μ mod 3, and ε_2(μ) = (-1)^{ν_2(μ)} is the character μ mod 4. l_1 is a central element (written l_1 = ε_1^2) and ν = (μ-1)/2. The page numbering is 5β1, and the equations are numbered (44)-(48), continuing (43) on the previous page.

(44) SG^*_{ρ,σ} is the set of triples (α,β,μ) in 𝔊' × 𝔊 × Ẑ^× satisfying two conditions:
- α ≡ τ^{ν_3(μ)} mod 𝔊, i.e. χ(α) = ε_3(μ);
- ξ := αρ(α)^{-1} = [α,ρ] equals ε_2(μ)·η·l_1^ν, where η := βσ(β)^{-1} = [β,σ].

This 'loop equation' (équation des lacets) is the analogue for hat SL2 / hat GL2 of the pentagon-type relation governing the GT action. The parity data are consistent:
- Since conjugation by τ inverts ρ and μ ≡ ε_3(μ) mod 6, we get ξρ = αρα^{-1}, which is conjugate to ρ^{ε_3(μ)} = ρ^μ.
- Since σ^{-1} = σ^3 = -σ, we have σ^μ = ε_2(μ)σ, so ε_2(μ)·βσβ^{-1} = βσ^μβ^{-1}.

(45) This gives a map SG^* → Σ_{ρ,σ} ⊂ 𝔊 × 𝔊 × Ẑ^×, where Σ_{ρ,σ} is the set of (ξ,η,μ) with:
- ξρ conjugate in 𝔊 to ρ^μ;
- ησ conjugate to σ^μ;
- ξ = η·l_1^ν.

The map is (α,β,μ) ↦ ([α,ρ], ε_2(μ)[β,σ], μ). By a corollary on p. 5β0, an 'effective' part Σ^{eff}_{ρ,σ} is isomorphic to a group B_{ρ,σ} (a braid-like group: hat B_3 or its GL analogue). G^{eff} is defined as the inverse image of Σ^{eff}, and the margin records an epimorphism SG^{eff} → Σ^{eff}. The fibres are torsors under the centralisers Z_ρ, Z_σ, extended by τ' to the groups N_ρ, N_σ of the previous page. This is why those normaliser-type groups and the epimorphisms δ_ρ, δ_σ were built.

(47) Grothendieck then enlarges to G^*_{ρ,σ} ⊂ G_{ρ,σ} × G_{ρ,σ} × Ẑ^×. It has the same commutator equation, with the parity condition relaxed to χ(α) = ε_3(μ)χ(β). He notes ξ = α(ρ)ρ^{-1} and η = ε_2(μ)β(σ)σ^{-1}.

(48) Then SG^* = G^* ∩ (𝔊' × 𝔊 × Ẑ^×). Equivalently, it is cut out from G^* by the two character conditions δ_σ(β) = 1 and δ_ρ(ατ^{ν_3(μ)}) = 1.

The next page constructs a section B_{ρ,σ} → G^{eff}, u ↦ (u, uτ^{ν_2(μ)}, χ_B(u)). So the triples (α,β,μ) are parametrised, up to centraliser torsors, by elements of the braid-like group. The underlying purpose is to describe the GT-like group, i.e. the automorphisms of the profinite SL2/GL2 amalgam fixing the conjugacy classes of ρ and σ up to μ-th powers, through pairs of conjugating elements subject to the loop equation.
errors: In (48), the second description reads '(α,β,μ) ∈ SG^*_{ρ,σ}'. This should be '∈ G^*_{ρ,σ}' (or G^{eff}), otherwise the description is circular. The next page's (50) indeed has '∈ G^{eff}'.
In (45) the defining relation of Σ is first written with a deleted factor and then as ξ = η l_1^ν. The ε_2(μ) is absorbed into η by the map, which is consistent but easy to misread.
The definition of SG^{eff} and of the surjectivity is left unfinished in the main text (sentence breaks off; the word 'surjective' is crossed out). The epimorphism is only asserted in the margin.

ideas.what: Parametrising automorphism-like data of the profinite SL2(Z) / GL2(Z) amalgam Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6 by triples (α,β,μ) with α, β conjugators for ρ, σ subject to a 'loop equation' [α,ρ] = ε_2(μ)[β,σ] l_1^{(μ-1)/2}
ideas.modern_name: GT-type description of automorphisms of the profinite completions of SL2(Z) / B_3 (Drinfeld–Ihara GT acting on hat B_3, hat SL2(Z))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; Lochak–Schneps (1990s) for GT acting on hat B_3 and hat SL2
ideas.where_published: Only hinted in Esquisse d'un programme / Longue Marche; the détails of 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' are unpublished

ideas.what: Map (α,β,μ) ↦ ([α,ρ], ε[β,σ], μ) to a set Σ of commutator invariants, identified with a braid-like group B_{ρ,σ}, with fibres torsors under centraliser/normaliser groups N_ρ, N_σ
ideas.modern_name: Fibration of the solution set of the GT equations over the braid group, via commutator coordinates

ideas.what: Careful sign/parity bookkeeping: χ(α) = ε_3(μ), σ^μ = ε_2(μ)σ, central correction l_1^{(μ-1)/2}

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up the GL2/SL2 analogue of the GT-defining equations: the solution set G^*_{ρ,σ}, its 'special' part SG^* and its 'effective' part G^{eff}. The effective part surjects onto a braid-group-like Σ^{eff} ≅ B_{ρ,σ}, with explicit centraliser-torsor fibres. This is a structured, sign-exact treatment of automorphisms of the profinite SL2(Z) amalgam that, as far as I know, was never published in this form.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could give an independent, GL2-equivariant formulation of the 'genus 1 / level 1' GT-type relations and of automorphisms of hat SL2(Z). Those relations are still studied (Lochak–Schneps, Enriquez's elliptic associators, Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki on hat SL2 automorphisms). The explicit sign conventions and the role of τ' (det -1) might be useful there.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but largely bookkeeping step in Grothendieck's unpublished 'loop equation' study for SL2/GL2 amalgams. The overall direction (GT acting on the profinite SL2 / B_3) is well known in later literature, but this precise parametrisation via commutator invariants and centraliser torsors is unpublished.
transcription_corrections: Equation numbers are (44), (45), [crossed (46)], (47), (48), continuing (43) on the previous page and leading to (49) on the next page; they are not (93)-(98).
Superscripts '#' should be '*' (G^*_{ρ,σ}, SG^*_{ρ,σ}), and '##' should be 'eff' (G^{eff}, Σ^{eff}), as on the next page.
In (44), the image reads 'α ≡ τ^{ν_3(μ)} mod 𝔊', not 'mod 𝔊''.
Page header is '5β1' (Grothendieck's own pagination), consistent with 'cor. p. 5β0'.
In (47), the first condition is χ(α) ≡ ε_3(μ)χ(β); the crossed-out symbol inside ε_3( ) should be ignored.
